per_pair.why: Game A's HUD is minimalist and clean with clear visual hierarchy; Game B clutters the screen with multiple information zones.
A's damage-taken animation is smooth and readable; B's competing elements make it hard to track the damage event.
A's pixel scaling and font rendering are perfect; B's UI elements have inconsistent sizing and visual weight.
A's low-health vignette integrates seamlessly; B's elements stack and overlap causing visual confusion.
A's element positioning leaves the action center-screen and readable; B's UI dominates viewport space and distracts from gameplay.
A demonstrates industry-standard clean UI design; B shows promise but needs dramatic simplification and reorganization.

loser_biggest_gap: Game B must reduce information clutter dramatically—consolidate the 5 competing UI elements (hearts, shards, boons, track, boss bar) into 2-3 visual zones with clear priority hierarchy, hide secondary information unless it's actively relevant, and adopt A's principle that the action must never be obscured.
loser_other_gaps: Pixel scaling and font rendering need consistency—A's integer-scaled sprites read cleanly; B's have sizing inconsistencies
Visual hierarchy is missing—no clear focal point tells the player what to watch; A uses position and emphasis to guide attention
Element animation timing is less polished—A's animations feel snappy; B's feel sluggish and cluttered
Color contrast and readability suffer under dense information load—A uses negative space effectively
reasoning: Game A sets the industry standard for clean, minimal UI that prioritizes gameplay clarity. Every element is intentional, positioned to avoid covering the action, and animated with crisp feedback. Game B's HUD is functionally complete but suffers from information overload—five distinct UI components all demanding attention simultaneously creates visual noise that competes with the gameplay itself. B needs to adopt A's philosophy: the screen is the player's window into the game world, and UI should guide attention, not hijack it.
